evals.prompt: I am adding a new authenticated HTTP endpoint. What must stay in sync with the OpenAPI spec?
evals.expected_behavior: The response identifies the handler, request/response schema, auth requirements, and invariants for keeping implementation and spec aligned.
assertions: Mentions both handler and OpenAPI/spec changes.
Mentions auth or error shape alignment.
Mentions invariants or anti-patterns for drift.

evals.prompt: I changed a response schema in a handler. Update the OpenAPI contract to match.
evals.expected_behavior: Before editing any file, the agent determines whether the repo is spec-first, code-first, or hybrid by reading repo docs, build targets, and generation tooling, then follows that specific contract path rather than assuming openapi.yaml is hand-edited.
assertions: Investigates whether the repo is spec-first, code-first, or hybrid before editing files.
Does not assume `openapi.yaml` is hand-maintained without checking for generation tooling.
Follows the repo-appropriate order (spec-first: spec then handlers; code-first: handler/types then regenerate).
deterministic_checks: identifies whether the repo is spec-first, code-first, or hybrid before making changes

evals.prompt: I added one optional query parameter to GET /orders. Update the contract for just that.
evals.expected_behavior: The agent updates only the affected operation's parameter definition (and regenerates if code-first) without rewriting unrelated paths, schemas, or the whole spec file.
assertions: Scopes the spec/contract change to the single new optional parameter on GET /orders.
Does not touch unrelated endpoints, schemas, or regenerate the entire spec beyond what changed.
Runs the repo's spec validation/generation step scoped to the change rather than a full-repo rebuild when a scoped one suffices.

evals.prompt: The code and OpenAPI document are drifting apart after a recent endpoint change. How should I fix it?
evals.expected_behavior: The response uses a source-of-truth-driven workflow, verifies both implementation and contract, and runs the repo's validation/generation step to reconcile the two rather than editing only one side.
assertions: Mentions identifying the contract owner / source of truth first.
Mentions verifying both implementation and contract, not just one.
Mentions running spec validation or generation as part of the fix.

evals.prompt: Generate a TypeScript client SDK from our existing openapi.yaml — nothing about the server or the spec itself is changing.
evals.expected_behavior: The response recognizes there is no server-contract change here, so the spec-sync workflow does not apply; it treats this as SDK/codegen tooling only, per the skill's own 'Do not use this skill when' list, and does not open unrelated handler or spec edits.
assertions: Does not run the spec-vs-handler drift-repair workflow when no server contract is changing.
Does not propose editing openapi.yaml or handlers as part of a client-only SDK generation request.
Treats the task as SDK/codegen generation, not contract synchronization.

evals.prompt: I refactored an internal helper function used by three background jobs. No HTTP endpoints or the OpenAPI spec are affected.
evals.expected_behavior: The response recognizes there is no HTTP contract surface in play and does not invent or touch an OpenAPI spec for internal-only code, per the skill's explicit out-of-scope case.
assertions: Does not add, edit, or invent OpenAPI spec content for code with no HTTP surface.
States plainly that no contract sync is needed for this change.
Does not force this skill's workflow onto a change with no HTTP/OpenAPI surface.

evals.prompt: The integration test for my HTTP route is failing after a middleware change. How should I debug it?
evals.expected_behavior: Runs the targeted integration test with verbose request/response output first and reads the real output before proposing any fix, per the documented first move.
assertions: Runs the targeted test with `-v` (or the repo's verbose flag) before proposing a fix
Reads the actual request/response output rather than guessing
Mentions middleware or auth interactions as the likely cause given the change
deterministic_checks: runs `go test -v -run TestE2E ./path/to/server/pkg/` (or equivalent targeted, verbose command) before proposing a fix

evals.prompt: I added POST /orders. Write the integration tests it needs.
evals.expected_behavior: Covers every concern the skill requires for a touched endpoint: status codes for happy path and documented errors, auth enforcement, request validation, response schema, and side effects.
assertions: Asserts the happy-path status code and documented error status codes
Asserts unauthenticated and invalid-token requests are rejected if the endpoint requires auth
Asserts missing/invalid request fields return a 400 with an error body
Asserts response schema (required fields, correct types) and relevant side effects (DB state, events)

evals.prompt: The whole integration suite went red after I added one new endpoint. What do I run first?
evals.expected_behavior: Runs the targeted test for the new endpoint first with verbose output, and only widens to the full suite if shared middleware or handlers were affected — not as the first step.
assertions: Runs the narrow, targeted test for the new/changed endpoint before the full suite
Only widens to the broader suite after confirming shared middleware/handlers are implicated
Does not rewrite unrelated existing tests while chasing this failure

evals.prompt: Write a test for this pure discount-calculation function — it doesn't touch HTTP at all.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes this is unit-level domain logic with no HTTP involvement and routes to testing-workflows rather than building an HTTP integration test.
assertions: Does not stand up an HTTP request/response test for pure domain logic
States this belongs to testing-workflows (the unit-test layer), not http-api
Does not add auth or endpoint-contract assertions that don't apply

evals.prompt: Update the OpenAPI description text for an existing field; no handler or behavior change.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes a spec-text-only change with no handler work, updates the contract, and does not start the integration-test workflow.
assertions: Does not add or modify integration tests for a spec-text-only change
Treats it as contract work only, without the integration-test workflow
Does not treat the spec edit as an endpoint contract change requiring new test coverage
